entries.clue: 2/6 in old money? (6,2,5)

blocks.note: the surface reads two shillings and sixpence, a half-crown price written the pre-1971 British way
the setter means a fraction: 30 old pence out of a 240-penny pound is one eighth, so such sums are portions of an eighth

annotation.surface: A price tag written in pre-decimal British currency.
annotation.walkthrough: Before decimalisation a pound held 240 pence, so 2/6 (30d) was exactly an eighth of a pound; the old Spanish dollar coins, pirates' treasure, share the name.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun: the phrase names historic Spanish coins, which is old money, and 2/6 is literally a piece of one eighth of a pound.

entries.clue: Tablet cover shows internet identification (2,7)

blocks.note: to dress is to cover (a body, a wound)

annotation.surface: A protective case for a tablet computer shows some online identifier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tablet cover' reads as a single accessory, but it splits into two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain technical description: the numeric label that picks out each device on a network is what identifies it on the internet.

entries.clue: Check in with a friend (5)

blocks.note: ch. is the chess abbreviation for check

annotation.surface: Keeping in touch by checking in with a friend.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is Cockney rhyming slang, where only the first word of the rhyming phrase is kept.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate, and the phrase is shortened to its first word.

entries.clue: Indication family member is unemployed (5,2)

blocks.note: a son is one member of a family

annotation.surface: A hint that one of the family is out of work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Indication family member' reads as one idea, a sign that a relative is jobless; it splits after the first word.
annotation.definitionFit: British idiom: registering at the job centre to claim benefit is what someone out of work does, so the phrase stands for being unemployed.

entries.clue: Settle for period film (7)

blocks.note: to foot the bill is to settle it
an age is a period of time

annotation.surface: Accepting a costume drama rather than something better.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Period film' looks like one phrase, a costume drama; 'period' belongs to the wordplay and 'film' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Film was once measured and sold by the foot, so recorded material came to be named after its length in feet.

entries.clue: At home, try partaking in drink that’s close by (2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.partaking in: to partake in something is to take part in it, to be inside it, so HEAR goes into the drink

blocks.note: tea, the drink, split around the next piece
a judge tries, or hears, a case

annotation.surface: Staying home and having a go at some drink nearby.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Try' here is the legal sense, as a court tries a case.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym phrase: whatever is somewhere in the neighbourhood is near at hand.

entries.clue: One wallowing in directorship position (5)

indicatorNotes.in: literally inside: the letters wanted lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: the tail of the first word runs into the head of the second

annotation.surface: Someone luxuriating in their boardroom role.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wallowing in' reads as a single verb phrase about enjoying a job; 'in' is doing the hiding.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by habit: the animal spends its days lolling in mud and rivers, so it is the creature best known for wallowing.

entries.clue: Eventually exhausted having fun (3,2,4,4)

annotation.surface: Worn out, in the end, from enjoying oneself.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eventually exhausted' reads as one phrase about tiring slowly; 'Eventually' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom urging patience: the thing will come when its moment arrives, which is to say later on.

entries.clue: Individual bedroom fitting you may be embarrassed about (3,5,5)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes the answer as something you may be embarrassed about

blocks.note: a bedside table, a fixture of the bedroom

annotation.surface: A piece of bedroom furniture you are ashamed of.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about furniture; the answer is a brief fling you might regret the morning after, still set in a bedroom.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a brief casual fling is the sort of thing people often regret or blush over the next morning.

entries.clue: It celebrates departure of an evil god destroyed (7,2)

indicatorNotes.destroyed: something destroyed is broken apart, so the letters are smashed and rebuilt in a new order

annotation.surface: A party to mark the end of a wicked deity.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is a British term for a farewell party thrown when someone leaves a job; 'do' is slang for a party.
annotation.definitionFit: British idiom: the office party thrown for someone quitting exists to mark their going, so it celebrates a departure.

entries.clue: On occasions, tramp didn’t get an easy score (3-2)

indicatorNotes.On occasions: something done on occasions happens only now and then, so only every other letter is taken

annotation.surface: A vagrant who failed to find a simple goal on the odd occasion.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is a football term; 'score' in the surface looks like a mark or tally.
annotation.definitionFit: A football term: a goal from so close the ball only needs tapping over the line is about as easy as scoring gets.

entries.clue: Country information I included in confidentiality contract (5)

indicatorNotes.included in: to be included in something is to sit within it, so the second I goes inside NDA

blocks.note: i is the symbol on tourist information signs
a non-disclosure agreement, split around the next piece

annotation.surface: A nation's data covered by a secrecy agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Information I' looks like one phrase, but information gives its own I and the clue's I is the one that goes inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the answer is one particular country in South Asia.

entries.clue: Attempt at extortion that will ruffle feathers? (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the second definition splits the word as SHAKE DOWN, a verb phrase

blocks.note: American slang for squeezing money out of someone by threats
read literally: agitate the soft underfeathers of a bird

annotation.surface: A blackmail attempt certain to upset people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ruffle feathers' means to upset people; the answer takes it literally, down being the fine feathers of a bird.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: slang for extortion by threat, and taken apart, a phrase for disturbing a bird's down, its fine feathers.

entries.clue: Such characters provide the beginnings of Picasso’s nuanced mural? (7)

annotation.definition: Such characters provide the beginnings of Picasso’s nuanced mural?

blocks.note: the surface suggests letters of some script in general, or people in a story

blocks.clueFragment: provide the beginnings of Picasso’s nuanced mural?
blocks.note: the setter means the openings PI-, NU- and MU-, each the name of a letter of one alphabet

annotation.surface: Describing the lettering an artist used to start a subtle wall painting.
annotation.walkthrough: PIcasso, NUanced and MUral start with PI, NU and MU, three letters of the Greek alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective means of ancient Greece, and pi, nu and mu are letters from that alphabet.

entries.clue: Popular English stage worker is a bit ungainly (9)

blocks.note: a leg is one stage of a journey or race

annotation.surface: A well-liked English stagehand is somewhat clumsy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stage worker' reads as a stagehand; it is two separate pieces, LEG and ANT.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: awkward, graceless movement lacks elegance, which is what both words describe.

entries.clue: Change page URL – it helps filter out rackets (7)

indicatorNotes.Change: to change something is to make it different, so the letters are put in a different order

annotation.surface: Web advice: alter the link on a page to block scam sites.
annotation.walkthrough: In the surface, rackets are online scams; in the definition they are loud noises.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: racket also means din, and the little plug in the ear exists to shut noise out.

entries.clue: Ringlet he adjusted making it more extended (9)

indicatorNotes.adjusted: to adjust something is to alter its arrangement, so the letters are moved about

annotation.surface: A hairdresser straightening a curl so it hangs longer.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is neat: pulling a curl straight really does make it hang further.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the comparative of 'lengthy', meaning stretched out further, longer.

entries.clue: Fuss by former pupil is disgusting (7)

indicatorNotes.by: by means beside, so SCENE is placed next to OB

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a school's former pupil
to make a scene is to make a fuss

annotation.surface: An old boy kicking up a fuss is a disgrace.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old boy' is the British term for a former pupil of a school.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: offensive to decency, repulsive.

entries.clue: Desire setter has is damaging (7)

blocks.note: the setter speaking of himself: I have, contracted

annotation.surface: The setter confesses a harmful craving.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter refers to himself, so 'setter has' becomes the contraction I'VE.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: wearing things gradually away is a kind of damage, as water does to rock.

entries.clue: Display stand for similar types of things (7)

annotation.definitionNote: the second definition is plural in form; the answer as in 'and so on' stands for things of that sort

blocks.note: a Victorian set of open shelves for ornaments
the vague tail of a list: 'books, papers and so on'

annotation.surface: Shop shelving meant for goods of a kind.
annotation.walkthrough: The furniture sense is a Victorian stand of open shelves for displaying small objects.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: an antique shelving stand for curios, and a catch-all word ending a list of similar items.

entries.clue: In attendance, contributing to WTO that’s questioning direction of travel (5,2)

indicatorNotes.contributing to: to contribute to something is to put your part into it, so HERE is put inside WTO

blocks.note: used as it stands, split around the next piece

annotation.surface: A delegate at the World Trade Organization querying its direction.
annotation.walkthrough: WTO, the World Trade Organization, is taken letter for letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by use: it is the question a taxi driver asks, about which way the journey should go.

entries.clue: Ferment noble rot and add energy for something sweet (9)

indicatorNotes.Ferment: to ferment is to churn and bubble, so the letters are stirred into a new order
indicatorNotes.add: to add is to put in extra, so E joins the letters before they are mixed

blocks.note: E = energy, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A winemaking recipe: ferment the grapes with noble rot to get a sweet wine.
annotation.walkthrough: Noble rot is the fungus behind sweet dessert wines, so 'something sweet' looks like a wine; it is a confection instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the triangular Swiss chocolate bar is one sweet among many.

entries.clue: Stink over honour – it may come as a surprise? (5)

annotation.definition: it may come as a surprise?

indicatorNotes.over: over means on top of, and in a down clue BO sits above MBE

blocks.note: Member of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour

annotation.surface: An award tainted by a scandal that nobody expected.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Surprise' is a menu word here: the domed ice-cream dessert is often served as a 'surprise' with a hidden centre.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example with a pun: the frozen dome is classically served as 'surprise', so it may come as one.

entries.clue: Composition of famous auteur writing from the heart (5)

indicatorNotes.from the heart: the heart is the centre, so the middle of each word is taken

annotation.surface: A great film-maker's heartfelt script.
annotation.walkthrough: Six-letter words give two middle letters and the seven-letter one gives one.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the short sacred choral piece is one kind of musical composition.

entries.clue: Queen’s speech perhaps initially made its appearance on wireless (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each following word is taken

annotation.surface: The monarch's annual address was first broadcast on radio.
annotation.walkthrough: A queen is a female cat; and the royal Christmas speech really did start on the wireless, old British for radio.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun with a crossword sense: a queen is also a female cat, and the sound a cat makes is its speech.

entries.clue: Degrees to which this creature is venomous? (5)

annotation.surface: Asking how venomous a certain animal is.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Degrees' is plural because it gives two: MA and MBA.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the African snake is one creature, and a notoriously venomous one.

entries.clue: Short article helping to create another version (9)

indicatorNotes.Short: something short is cut down, so ITEM loses its last letter

blocks.note: ITEM, an article, without its last letter
a ration is a helping, a portion

annotation.surface: A brief piece of writing helps produce a new edition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like a verb joining the parts; it is a noun, a portion.
annotation.definitionFit: Software and design jargon: each repeated round of revision produces a new release, one more version.

entries.clue: Footballer to send on after midpoint (6,7)

indicatorNotes.after: after means following, so FORWARD comes behind CENTRE

blocks.note: to forward a letter is to send it on

annotation.surface: A player about to be sent on after half-time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Send on' reads as bringing on a substitute; it means to redirect mail.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the attacking player leading the line is one position a footballer plays.
